question: We are building a CV-screening tool that ranks job applicants for our clients. What applies to us under the AI Act?

final.answer:
Your CV-screening tool is classified as a high-risk AI system because it is intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons [AI Act Art. 6(2); AI Act Annex III, point 4]. Even if an AI system is listed in Annex III, it is not considered high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm to fundamental rights, but this exception does not apply if the system performs profiling of natural persons [AI Act Art. 6(3)]. As a provider of a high-risk AI system, you must ensure compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2 [AI Act Art. 16(a)]. You are required to indicate your contact details on the system or its documentation, maintain a quality management system, keep required documentation, and preserve logs automatically generated by the system [AI Act Art. 16(b); AI Act Art. 16(c); AI Act Art. 16(d); AI Act Art. 16(e)]. Furthermore, you must ensure the system undergoes a conformity assessment, draw up an EU declaration of conformity, affix the CE marking, and comply with registration obligations [AI Act Art. 16(f); AI Act Art. 16(g); AI Act Art. 16(h); AI Act Art. 16(i)]. You must also take necessary corrective actions, demonstrate conformity upon request by a national authority, and ensure the system complies with accessibility requirements [AI Act Art. 16(j); AI Act Art. 16(k); AI Act Art. 16(l)]. The GDPR applies to your tool because the processing of personal data must be lawful [GDPR Art. 6]. Processing is only lawful if it meets specific conditions, such as the data subject's consent, the performance of a contract, compliance with a legal obligation, the protection of vital interests, the performance of a task in the public interest, or the pursuit of legitimate interests [GDPR Art. 6].

This is information about the texts, not legal advice.

steps.summary: The CV-screening tool is classified as a high-risk AI system under the AI Act, specifically falling under Annex III, point 4, which covers AI systems intended to be used for recruitment or selection of natural persons. As a provider of this system, you are subject to the high-risk requirements set out in the regulation, including obligations related to risk management, data governance, and technical documentation.

As a provider of a high-risk AI system for recruitment, you are subject to comprehensive obligations under Article 16 of the AI Act. These include establishing a quality management system, maintaining technical documentation and logs, undergoing conformity assessments, and ensuring compliance with registration, CE marking, and accessibility requirements.

The GDPR applies to your CV-screening tool because the processing of personal data for recruitment must satisfy the lawfulness requirements of GDPR Article 6. Specifically, your data governance obligations under AI Act Article 10 for training and testing data must align with the legal bases for processing personal data, such as contract performance or legitimate interests, as defined in the GDPR.
